stand: Iran's IRGC continues near-daily strikes and turn-back orders against tankers in Hormuz; the week of 28 September-5 October saw at least 12 tanker attacks, the highest weekly total since the war began, while the IMO recorded nine. On 6 October a projectile hit tanker On Peace, injuring 12 crew, 11 Indian. An IRGC adviser says Iran will soon block 'illegal' smuggling routes off Oman's coast and claims full control of the strait. Gulf exports remain elevated, topping pre-war levels on about 14 days in September per Kpler.

claims.text: Gulf crude exports topped pre-war levels on about 14 days in September, roughly half the month, per Kpler data; Iran's IRGC continues to dispute the significance of this recovery.
claims.by: Says: Kpler ship-tracking data, via Reuters. Denies/minimises: IRGC adviser Majid Mirahmadi, who says transits remain far below pre-war levels.

claims.text: A Kpler analyst speculates Gulf states may be paying Iran a toll for safe tanker passage through Hormuz; Lloyd's List reported the IRGC already running a 'toll booth' system since March. Washington says it will not permit any toll under a deal.
claims.by: Says: Kpler's Michelle Brohard (speculation); Lloyd's List (March report). Rejects: Trump administration, which says Iran will not be allowed to charge a toll under any agreement.

claims.text: IRGC commander Ali Fadavi's claim that US naval forces have withdrawn 1,000km from Iran's borders was echoed by a second official, who said foreign warships have moved more than 1,000km from the Gulf and 'do not dare approach'.
claims.by: Says: IRGC commander Ali Fadavi; IRGC political bureau deputy Yadollah Javani (via IRNA). Denies: CENTCOM, which reports active blockade enforcement and US naval interdictions as recently as 5 October.

claims.text: The IRGC Navy has warned ships using the US-supervised southern route through Hormuz that they may be targeted at any point.
claims.by: Says: IRGC, via commander Ali Fadavi.

claims.text: The attack tally has widened: JMIC counts nearly 20 commercial ships attacked in Hormuz, the Gulf or off Oman over the past month, beyond the week-long UKMTO count already logged.
claims.by: Says: Joint Maritime Information Center.

claims.text: On 5 October the IRGC twice hailed inbound tankers near Oman and ordered them to turn back or be targeted; both masters complied.
claims.by: Says: UKMTO.

claims.text: US CENTCOM says it has redirected 130 commercial vessels, disabled three and destroyed 13 over the past 12 weeks while enforcing its blockade on ships entering or leaving Iranian ports.
claims.by: Says: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper.

claims.text: The ICC warns that if Hormuz shipping restrictions persist, grain prices in some regions could rise by up to 80%, driven largely by disrupted fertiliser supply chains.
claims.by: Says: ICC Secretary-General John Denton.

claims.text: Kuwait's oil output has recovered to about 75% of pre-war levels as more tankers risk Hormuz transits, says Kuwait Petroleum Corp's chief executive.
claims.by: Says: Sheikh Nawaf Al-Sabah, CEO, Kuwait Petroleum Corp.

claims.text: LNG shipments through Hormuz are rebounding but remain more than 75% below pre-war levels.
claims.by: Says: Bloomberg/Kpler ship-tracking data.

claims.text: Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company transported two million barrels of crude through the Strait of Hormuz on a VLCC, its first such operation in decades.
claims.by: Says: Iraq's Oil Tanker Company (director general).

claims.text: A projectile struck the Panama-flagged tanker MT On Peace in the Strait of Hormuz on 6 October, injuring 12 of its 19 crew, 11 of them Indian; Oman evacuated the wounded to Khasab. India did not identify the attacker.
claims.by: Says: India's Ministry of External Affairs; Oman's Ministry of Defence.

claims.text: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority has blacklisted the tanker On Peace for allegedly violating Iranian transit protocols and threatens listed vessels with fines, detention or confiscation.
claims.by: Says: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, per gCaptain.

claims.text: Trump claims Iran's oil minister has quit, quoting the official as saying Iran has no economy and no oil left.
claims.by: Says: US President Donald Trump.

claims.text: The ICC is working with the UN and IMO on a plan to temporarily place Hormuz navigation under UN management, but US-Iran tensions have stalled it.
claims.by: Says: International Chamber of Commerce, per Wall Street Journal.

claims.text: Oil and condensate exports through the Strait of Hormuz reached about 75% of pre-conflict levels in the week of 26 September-2 October.
claims.by: Says: Euler analyst Andrey Polishchuk, via TASS.

claims.text: Gulf oil flows excluding Iran rose above 81% of pre-war levels in September, led by Saudi exports, while Iran's own exports fell to zero under the US blockade.
claims.by: Says: gCaptain, citing tracking data.

claims.text: An IRGC adviser says Iran will soon block 'illegal' routes hugging Oman's coast used to smuggle oil, and claims the Strait of Hormuz is under Iran's full control.
claims.by: Says: IRGC adviser Mohammadreza Naqdi (Fars News Agency), also reported by TASS as 'Mohammad Reza Naghdi'.

claims.text: IRGC adviser Majid Mirahmadi says only an average of 10 ships a day now transit Hormuz, against 125 a day before the war, disputing the narrative of recovering Gulf flows.
claims.by: Says: IRGC adviser Majid Mirahmadi.

claims.text: Maritime security sources tracking incidents say the week of 28 September-5 October saw at least 12 tanker attacks in and around Hormuz, the highest weekly tally since the war began on 28 February.
claims.by: Says: three maritime security sources, via Reuters.

claims.text: The UN shipping agency IMO recorded nine incidents involving vessels in Hormuz the same week, 28 September-5 October.
claims.by: Says: International Maritime Organization.

timeline.text: US-Israel war on Iran began, the starting point for the Hormuz crisis.
US naval blockade against Iran resumes.
Attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, later cited as a driver of the export surge.
Kazimah III last seen discharging Kuwaiti crude at Ras Markaz, Oman, before being struck days later.
Maritime security sources log at least 12 tanker attacks in Hormuz, the highest weekly tally since the war began; the IMO separately records nine incidents.
Crude exports from the region exceeded pre-war levels on four days.
Seven-day moving average for regional crude exports reaches 18.3 million bpd.
Kpler data show Gulf crude exports topped pre-war levels on 14 days in September.
VLCC Kazimah III struck by a projectile in the strait, causing an onboard fire.
Seven-day moving average for crude exports rises to 18.5 million bpd.
UKMTO begins reporting at least one attack per day in Hormuz or the Gulf of Aden.
JMIC documents four confirmed tanker attacks in the strait, along the Omani side.
A crude oil tanker is struck above the waterline during transit; timing unclear, possibly overlapping other reports.
Iraq's Oil Tanker Company announces its first VLCC transit of the strait in decades, carrying two million barrels of crude.
Aframax tanker Lipsi struck near Jazirat Um Al Fayarin, Oman, damaging its engine room.
UKMTO reports a separate tanker hit by an unknown projectile within Hormuz.
A tanker north of Khasab, Oman, is hailed by the IRGC and ordered to turn back; the master complies.
A tanker transiting the strait is struck by an unknown projectile at 1637 UTC, causing an engine-room fire.
CENTCOM says US forces redirected the 130th commercial vessel under the blockade.
IRGC commander Ali Fadavi says US forces have fled 1,000km from Iran's borders.
Kuwait Petroleum Corp's CEO says output has recovered to 75% of pre-war levels.
ICC Secretary-General warns Hormuz restrictions could push grain prices up by as much as 80%.
Kpler analyst Michelle Brohard speculates in an interview that Gulf states may be paying Iran a toll for safe passage.
Panama-flagged tanker On Peace struck by a projectile off Khasab/Limah, Oman; 12 of 19 crew injured, 11 Indian; Oman evacuates wounded to Khasab.
India's foreign ministry condemns the attack and calls for an immediate end to strikes on shipping and seafarers.
Trump says oil is flowing through Hormuz at or above pre-war levels and claims Iran's oil minister has resigned.
Euler estimates Hormuz crude and condensate exports recovered to about 75% of pre-conflict levels for 26 Sep-2 Oct.
JMIC tallies nearly 20 commercial ships attacked in Hormuz, the Gulf or off Oman over the past month.
IRGC adviser Mohammadreza Naqdi says Iran will soon block 'illegal' smuggling routes off Oman's coast and claims full control of the Strait of Hormuz.
IRGC political bureau deputy Yadollah Javani repeats the claim that foreign warships have retreated more than 1,000km from the Gulf.
Lloyd's List reports the IRGC had already imposed a toll system on vessel traffic through Hormuz.
